raw_response:
I have been farming these 7.7 mu for forty years, and at seventy I know every inch of this soil. My household has five people, so we still have the hands to manage a little cotton, but I am not young anymore—I need crops that can be mechanized where possible. The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn; this is Quzhou, after all, and winter wheat followed by summer maize is how we make our living. I keep 5 mu in that double-crop system because it is reliable and the machines can do the heavy work. The remaining 2.7 mu I plant to cotton. It is labor-intensive, especially the picking, but my family helps and the income from cotton still pays for school fees and medicine better than grain alone.

For the wheat already growing: I use an improved semi-dwarf variety I have trusted for years. I will topdress nitrogen at regreening and again at jointing, and I will irrigate four times total—overwinter, regreening, jointing, and grain filling—using my well. I apply phosphorus and potassium as base dressing. Two sprays will do: one herbicide and one fungicide/insecticide mix.

For summer maize: As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I plant a hybrid maize variety directly into the wheat stubble without ploughing. No-tillage saves moisture and time, and every day matters before the autumn cold. I side-dress nitrogen at the big-flare stage and irrigate three times. Two pesticide applications are enough with good hybrids.

For cotton: I deep-plough the 2.7 mu in spring because cotton likes a loose, deep seedbed. I plant an improved Bt variety under plastic mulch to warm the soil and hold moisture. Cotton needs more potassium than grain crops, so I give it plenty. I irrigate three times and spray four times for aphids and mites that the Bt does not control. We will pick it by hand in autumn.
